contents.reason: The weak-* to compact-uniform openness of the extreme-point quotient is not needed: the primitivity of the algebra viewpoint is not used on this page, and no scaffolded item or consumer invokes the quotient map from extremal positive type functions to the dual.

contents.name: Propositions 1.C.10–1.C.12 (functoriality of the Fell topology: dense images, automorphisms, closed normal subgroups)
contents.reason: Functoriality for homomorphisms and normal subgroups is representation-restriction machinery later pages (RG-23–RG-30) can call on; this page fixes the topology and its closure property only, and no scaffolded item consumes these functoriality statements.

contents.name: Proposition 1.D.1 and Remarks 1.D.2/1.D.5 (local quasi-compactness and the Baire property of Ĝ)
contents.reason: Local quasi-compactness is proved through weak-* compactness of P≤1(G) and a convexity argument; no item on this page needs it, and the Fell-discreteness corollary for compact groups is proved independently by orthogonality of coefficients.

contents.name: Propositions 1.D.3–1.D.4 (second countability of the dual of a second-countable group)
contents.reason: Second countability of the dual is a separable-C*-algebra statement whose consumer belongs to the later direct-integral and type-I page; the present page makes no countability assumption and no scaffolded item depends on it.

contents.name: Propositions 1.D.6–1.D.7 (the dual of an LCA group is locally compact; discrete/compact duality)
contents.reason: LCA duality and the topology of the character group are constructed and proved on the published character-groups page; this page only records the seam and recomputes C*(G) ≅ C0(Ĝ), so the statements are deferred rather than duplicated.

contents.name: Proposition 1.D.8 and Remark 1.D.9 (the dual of a compact group is discrete)
Examples 1.D.10 and 1.D.14 (a non-compact group with countable dual; a non-discrete group with quasi-compact dual)
contents.reason: Both computations rest on the Mackey machine for induced representations and on Pontryagin duality of p-adic or compact normal subgroups; induction is owned by RG-23/RG-24 and neither example is used by any item on this page.

contents.name: Proposition 1.D.12 (the dual of a discrete group is quasi-compact)
contents.reason: Quasi-compactness of the dual of a discrete group follows from weak-* compactness of P1 and is not used by any scaffolded item; the page's compact-group statement concerns discreteness of the dual, which is a different direction.

contents.name: Theorem 1.D.15 and Remark 1.D.16 (T0/T1 of the dual iff type I/CCR; closed points)
